The C.I.P. designation for the 76 mm (3 in) shell.

aliases.name: 36 gauge
aliases.note: The alternative name C.I.P. records on the datasheet, and the usual continental European designation. The gauge arithmetic does not quite work: a true 36-gauge bore would be about 0.506 in.

boreDiameter.sourceNote: Bore diameter of the SAAMI 410 bore standard smoothbore velocity and pressure test barrel, .410 in +.005.

caseLength.sourceNote: Cartridge maximum for the 410/63,5 shell, dimension l. This is the fired length of the unfolded case, which the chamber must accept; the same datasheet lists 50.7, 65, 69.8, 72.8 and 76 mm shells sharing every other dimension.

overallLength.sourceNote: Loaded length of the roll-crimped 2½ in shell, 2.400 in, from the SAAMI 410 Bore 2½ in cartridge and chamber drawing. The folded-crimp figure on the same drawing is 2.360 in.

maxPressure.sourceNote: Pmax for the 410/63,5 shell, 830 bar. The 72.8 and 76 mm shells are rated at 1050 bar on the same sheet.

bulletMass.sourceNote: 109 gr as published, converted to grams. A quarter of an ounce, in a 2½ in shell.

barrelLength.sourceNote: Federal publishes this velocity without naming a test barrel. SAAMI Z299.2 specifies a 26.000 in (660.40 mm) standard smoothbore barrel for 410 bore velocity and pressure work, and the figure is recorded on the basis that a SAAMI member measures in it.

images.alt: Six empty .410 bore cases lying on a pale wooden surface: four with green plastic hulls and brass heads, and two plain nickel-coloured all-metal cases, one of them standing upright showing its primer and headstamp.
images.caption: Fired .410 bore cases, plastic-hulled and all-metal. The mouths are open because the crimp unfolds when the shell is fired; a loaded round is shorter than the case length it is named for.

images.alt: Two all-metal .410 cases beside a .22 Long Rifle cartridge, with a steel rule at the right. One .410 case stands upright showing its open mouth; the other lies on its side showing the headstamp W C C 52. The .410 cases are about three times the diameter of the rimfire round.
images.caption: Two M35 all-metal .410 cases with a .22 Long Rifle cartridge for scale. Cases of this type were issued with the M6 aircrew survival gun, which is why the headstamp is a military one; commercial .410 shells are plastic or paper over a brass head.
